thread:
irene: 08:14 — heads up: seeing an uptick of 504s from hosted inference in eu-west-1. Errors started ~08:10, customer tickets piling up for /v1/generate timeouts. war room?

sanjay_oncall: 08:15 — I'm oncall. Looking at grafana now — 504 error-rate jumped to ~12% across the gateway cluster. p50 latency doubled.

maya_engsre: 08:16 — pulling gateway logs. sample:
```
gateway-frontend-3 | 2024-11-06T08:12:34Z | upstream read timeout after 30s | proxy: 504
```
queued requests show long tails. any recent deploys?

alex_support: 08:17 — Support queue: multiple customers report hangs then 504. No auth or billing changes reported. Affected customers: acct-5689, acct-1290, acct-7744.

deploy-bot: 08:18 — deploy:service/gateway rolling deployment completed 07:58 by ci/cd pipeline.

sanjay_oncall: 08:19 — I'll roll the gateway canary back to previous revision to rule out a bad deploy. Kicking rollback.

ops-bot: 08:21 — rollback started (id: rollback-abc123).

sanjay_oncall: 08:25 — rollback finished. immediate improvement: 504s dropped from 12% -> 6%. baseline is ~0.5% though, so still elevated. investigating upstream inference pools.

maya_engsre: 08:30 — checking inference pool metrics. Found a dramatic increase in long-sequence requests from acct-5689 starting ~08:08. KV cache miss rate spiked, memory churn high; queue length on hosted-pool-7 > 20s. Looks like single-tenant burst.

irene: 08:31 — support confirms acct-5689 ran a test harness sending 10k-token prompts in bulk.

sanjay_oncall: 08:33 — applying temporary mitigations: throttling offending IP block and routing heavy requests to burst-capable dedicated nodes. temp ip block rule applied: 
```
# temporary block
iptables -I INPUT -s 3.12.45.0/24 -j DROP
```
also adding a router rule to divert seq>4096 to dedicated-burst pool.

maya_engsre: 08:37 — tweaked KV cache eviction thresholds and lowered hosted pool max-seq-length to 2048 for new requests. seeing p50/p95 drop toward normal over ~8-12m.

alex_support: 08:49 — acct-5689 acknowledged, paused tests. told impacted customers we'll follow up with credits.

julie_product: 09:05 — notes from product: single-tenant noisy neighbor problem — need per-customer seq-length caps, better quota on token-length, and a graceful queue-shedding strategy so a single tenant can't saturate hosted pools.

sanjay_oncall: 09:10 — drafting postmortem + action items. immediate list (owners + due dates):
- enforce per-account concurrent request cap (owner: maya_engsre, due: 2024-12-02)
- implement per-account max-sequence-length at edge (owner: infra-team, due: 2025-01-10)
- auto-detect KV-cache thrash and fallback to lower-context model (owner: sanjay_oncall, due: 2025-01-15)
- improve routing so noisy tenants are routed into isolated burst pools (owner: infra-team, due: 2025-02-28)
- add alert/graph for per-tenant seq-length distribution (owner: observability, due: 2024-11-20)

irene: 09:12 — logging incident, creating customer credits for SLA violations. estimated impacted requests ~1.2k over 25 minutes.

maya_engsre: 09:20 — attaching graphs, KV heap snapshots, and request traces to the PM: https://redwood.internal/pm/2387654321. also saved firewall rules and rollback artifacts.

sanjay_oncall: 09:45 — postmortem draft published: https://docs.redwood/incident/2387654321 — please review for technical accuracy and add remediation tasks.

irene: 10:10 — closing war room. followups tracked in the PM doc and sprint board. thanks all :tada: Please ping if anything regresses.

ops-bot: 10:11 — incident-status: resolved (runbook: host-inference-504-spike).
